# Carl Meredith

## Overview

- **Age:** Ten years old  <sub>[v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c33 P30](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0030), [v5 c31 P23](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0023)</sub>
- **Origin:** Maywater  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>

## Appearance

Carl is a young boy with a white face and eyes that closely resemble his deceased mother's.

_Sources: [v5 c33 P30](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0030), [v5 c31 P23](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0023)_

## Personality

Carl is a brave, game, and observant boy who bears punishments unflinchingly to save his father distress. He possesses a deep fascination for nature and small creatures, patiently spending time studying them. He is willing to endure personal discomfort and strict self-imposed discipline to maintain his sense of honor.

_Sources: [v5 c33 P12](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0012), [v5 c33 P13](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0013), [v5 c33 P27](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0027), [v5 c31 P22](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0022)_

## Traits

- Brave  <sub>[v5 c33 P13](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0013), [v5 c33 P27](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0027)</sub>
- Observant of nature  <sub>[v5 c33 P12](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0012)</sub>
- Honorable  <sub>[v5 c31 P22](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0022)</sub>

## Abilities

- Studying insects and small animals  <sub>[v5 c33 P12](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0012), [v5 c14 P38](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0038)</sub>

## History

Carl grew up in Maywater with his siblings before moving to the manse in Glen St. Mary. He became an active member of his family's Good-Conduct Club, through which the children managed their own behavior and discipline. After being dared by older boys, he placed a large eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy under the impression that it was dead, causing her horse to bolt when the eel revived; his father called him into the study for a whipping, but John Meredith ultimately could not bring himself to strike him upon seeing Carl's mother's eyes in his face. To punish himself for perceived cowardice in an earlier incident involving a ghost story, Carl sat on Mr. Pollock's tombstone in the graveyard until midnight during a freezing rainstorm. This exposure caused him to contract severe double pneumonia, bringing him near death before Dr. Blythe and a nurse successfully nursed him through the crisis. Upon his recovery, the local children and Dr. Blythe celebrated his health with a special feast and fireworks in Rainbow Valley.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c33 P12](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0012), [v5 c33 P16](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0016), [v5 c33 P30](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0030), [v5 c33 P31](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0031), [v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020), [v5 c31 P22](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0022), [v5 c31 P27](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0027), [v5 c31 P29](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0029), [v5 c31 P32](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0032)_

## Quotes

> The boys were fishing for eels over the bridge. Link Drew had caught a whopper—I mean an awful big one—the biggest eel I ever saw. He caught it right at the start and it had been lying in his basket a long time, still as still. I thought it was dead, honest I did. Then old Mrs. Carr drove over the bridge and she called us all young varmints and told us to go home. And we hadn’t said a word to her, father, truly. So when she drove back again, after going to the store, the boys dared me to put Link’s eel in her buggy. I thought it was so dead it couldn’t hurt her and I threw it in. Then the eel came to life on the hill and we heard her scream and saw her jump out. I was awful sorry. That’s all, father.  <sub>[v5 c33 P16](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0016)</sub>

> I forgot. Besides, I didn’t think any harm came of it. I didn’t know she jarred her legs. But I’m to be whipped and that will make things square.  <sub>[v5 c33 P25](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0025)</sub>

> Oh, not so much, I guess. Anyhow, I’m not going to cry, no matter how much it hurts. It would make father feel so bad, if I did. He’s all cut up now. I wish I could whip myself hard enough and save him doing it.  <sub>[v5 c33 P27](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0027)</sub>

> He—he didn’t whip me at all, and—I wish he had—and he’s in there, feeling just awful.  <sub>[v5 c33 P35](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0035)</sub>

> That—tombstone—over here, it’s—moving—about—it’s coming—at—me—keep it—away—please.  <sub>[v5 c31 P25](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0025)</sub>
